terms.gloss: beds set one above the other
terms.grammar: plural of lectus, lectī m., with the participle of superpōnō
terms.comment: A description of ours: Morgan–Owens has the heading “bunk bed” with no Latin, and we found none in Traupman or Levi–Bini. Superpōnere is to set one thing on another (Livy, Columella; Lewis & Short). The top bunk is lectus superior, the bottom one lectus īnferior.

phrases.latin: Tū in lectō superiōre dormiēs, frāter in īnferiōre.
phrases.english: You’ll sleep in the top bunk, your brother in the bottom one.

phrases.latin: Cavē nē dē lectō superiōre dēcidās!
phrases.english: Mind you don’t fall out of the top bunk!

sources: Lewis & Short: lectus · Lewis & Short: superpono
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. bed: bunk bed.
